items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Customer concentration in fiscal 2026: four customers

set.signal: Customer concentration in fiscal 2026: four customers were 10% or more of total revenue - Cisco at 20%, NVIDIA at 16%, Nokia at 11% and Amazon at 11%. CFO Csaba Sverha: 'In 2026, we continued to diversify our customer base.'

items.reason: NVIDIA 'down 20%+ for the year' and 'the rest of the business up nearly 60%' are analyst Tim Savageaux's words (Tim Long: 'pretty good decline'); management never confirmed them, and the ~60% is arithmetic.
items.evidence: Tim Savageaux: ... congrats on growing mid-30s with NVIDIA down 20%+ for the year. I think that's the rest of the business up nearly 60% on that basis.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: NVIDIA was Fabrinet's second-largest customer at 16%

set.signal: NVIDIA was a 10%+ customer at 16% of fiscal 2026 revenue. Asked about this customer, CEO Seamus Grady said Fabrinet is optimistic about sequential data center growth in Q1 FY2027 'both with longstanding customers, like the one you mentioned, and newer customers', and declined to speak on behalf of the customer or its suppliers on specific components. Asked about 1.6T timing for the largest Datacom customer, he referred the question to NVIDIA: 'You'd have to talk to NVIDIA about the NVIDIA product launches.'

items.reason: The YoY decline (>20%) and its causes (component constraints, program maturity) are analysts' statements (Tim Long, Tim Savageaux); management never confirmed them. 'Second-largest' is inferred from the ranking.
items.evidence: Csaba Sverha: These were Cisco at 20%, NVIDIA at 16%, Nokia at 11%, and Amazon at 11% of total revenue.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capacity roadmap raised from the ~$11.5 billion figure

set.signal: Capacity roadmap: CEO Seamus Grady said Fabrinet has 'land capacity and plans in place' to bring revenue capacity up to between $12.5 billion and $14 billion over the coming years. Bridge from the $5.3 billion run rate exiting Q4 FY2026 ($1.32B x 4): Pinehurst office-to-manufacturing conversion of 120,000 sq ft takes it to $5.5-$5.8B; Building 10 in Chonburi (2 million sq ft, complete by early 2027, 250,000 sq ft qualified on floor one with a similar amount on floor three qualifying this quarter) adds $3.0-$3.5B to reach $8.5-$9.3B; the newly commissioned Navanakorn building (200,000 sq ft, contributing from Q1) adds $200-$250M; the newly acquired Great America Place campus in Santa Clara (~130,000 sq ft of manufacturing, more than doubling the Silicon Valley footprint) adds $200-$250M; and two more Chonburi factories of ~1.2 million sq ft each add $1.8-$2.1B. Asked how this compares with last quarter's figure, Grady cited added square footage (Navanakorn, Santa Clara and other additions) and rising revenue per square foot, driven by revenue-dense DCI product and better space utilization. Fabrinet continues to look for more land.

items.reason: The ~$11.5 billion 'last quarter' figure is analyst George Notter's recollection ('if I have that correct'); management did not state or confirm it.
items.evidence: George Notter: I think last quarter when you discussed this, I think you kind of circulated or centered on an $11.5 billion revenue run rate, if I have that correct.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Multi-rail optical architectures are a new engagement area

set.signal: Multi-rail optical architectures: CEO Seamus Grady said they package and manage fiber pairs as a highly integrated optical system, creating more photonics integration and manufacturing complexity per deployment - dense fiber routing and management, high-volume fusion splicing and connectorization, and precision optical assembly. Fabrinet is heavily engaged on a number of multi-rail programs with customers and sees them as a strong fit for its process-step 'secret sauce.' Grady noted customers do not necessarily share where the products end up, but management believes Fabrinet is participating in scale-up, scale-out and scale-across, with DCI specifically serving scale-out and scale-across.

items.reason: 'New market opportunity' was the analyst's framing (Ryan Koontz), not management's; the CEO's hedge on customer visibility was lost.
items.evidence: Seamus Grady: Again, bear in mind our customers don't necessarily share with us their plans for where all of the products we make for them are going to end up.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: On the proposed U.S. ban on new Chinese transceivers

set.signal: On the proposed ban on new transceivers from China: not a done deal and early days, but Fabrinet does not manufacture for any Chinese providers and is focused on Western providers, so in theory it should be a positive - as long as materials and components are available. Grady cautioned that a large share of transceivers going into data centers today come from China, so an outright ban would bring the whole industry to a halt.

items.reason: The call never says the ban is a U.S. one; that is background knowledge.
items.evidence: Seamus Grady: The proposed ban on new transceivers from China, I guess it's not yet a done deal.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Revenue reporting was recast into three end-market categories

set.signal: Revenue reporting was recast into three end-market categories from Q4 FY2026 onward: (1) data centers, (2) communications infrastructure, (3) automotive, industrial and other. The prior categories were replaced because hyperscalers and other data center service providers are the ultimate customers of many products previously characterized as telecom. CFO Csaba Sverha: the thumb rule is 'whatever the product's getting deployed, if it's a data center or hyperscale, then it goes in the data center, everything else goes into the communication infrastructure.' A 12-quarter history under the new structure was posted; the change is presentational only with no impact on total revenue in any period.

items.reason: The call does not name an 'optical/non-optical' split; that is background knowledge.
items.evidence: Seamus Grady: hyperscalers and other data center service providers are the ultimate customers of many of the products we manufacture, including some of those that have been characterized as telecom products in the past.

items.label: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 (08-17-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Balance sheet and cash flow: cash and short-term investments ended

set.signal: Balance sheet and cash flow: cash and short-term investments ended the quarter at $876 million, down $70 million sequentially. Operating cash flow was $55 million and CapEx rose to $92 million (Building 10 construction plus $11 million for the Navanakorn campus), leaving free cash flow at an outflow of $37 million. Full-year operating cash flow was $257 million and full-year free cash flow $4 million. Inventory rose on revenue growth and on positioning material for upcoming customer ramps rather than on a step-change in component constraints.
set.figure: $876M cash+STI; Q4 OCF $55M; Q4 CapEx $92M; Q4 FCF -$37M; FY OCF $257M; FY FCF $4M
